title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 72
paragraphs: Leotychides, however, did not himself live out his old age in Sparta; he paid a penalty for what had been done to Demaratus, and this is how. He went as commander of the Lacedaemonians on a campaign into Thessaly, and although he could have reduced the whole country to subjection, he accepted a large bribe instead. He was caught in the act right there in camp, sitting on a glove stuffed full of money. Brought to trial, he was exiled from Sparta and his house was razed to the ground. He went into exile at Tegea and ended his life there.
